# Data card

## Synthetic analytics database (`data/creatorops.sqlite`)

**All of this data is fake.** It is generated by `scripts/generate_analytics_db.py` (seed 42 by default),
so anyone can rebuild exactly the same database. The file itself is not committed.

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| `platforms` | Instagram, TikTok, YouTube |
| `creators` | 8 generic personas ("Creator A", fashion, FR...) |
| `accounts` | one account per creator per platform, with follower counts |
| `brands` | 10 invented brands with a category (beauty, alcohol, supplements...) |
| `campaigns` | 2-3 brand campaigns per creator |
| `posts` | ~1400 posts from 2026-05-01 to 2026-10-31 (format, caption, paid, disclosure) |
| `post_metrics_daily` | metrics for the first 7 days of each post |
| `schedule`, `approvals` | upcoming posts and their approval status |
| `contracts_index` | one contract per campaign, links to the synthetic contract documents |

How the numbers are made:
- reach depends on followers, post format (Reels reach more than photos), a seasonal factor
  (summer higher, September lower) and random noise (log-normal)
- engagement rate depends on the format, sponsored posts do a bit worse

Planted anomalies (so analytics questions have a clear answer):
1. a viral Reel for Creator C in July 2026 (about 15x the normal reach)
2. fake engagement for Creator F on 2026-08-12 (likes jump, reach does not)
3. a slump for Creator E in August 2026 (reach about 40% lower)
4. two paid Instagram posts without a disclosure label (both by Creator B)

Limitations: the distributions are simple and only roughly realistic. They are good enough to test SQL and
hybrid questions, not to draw real marketing conclusions.

## Document corpus (`data/manifest.csv`)

Built by `scripts/download_corpus.py` from `data/sources.csv`. Raw files are not committed (`data/raw/`),
only the manifest. 158 documents, 170 files (some documents have several dated snapshots).

| Group | Documents | Source | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instagram / Meta policies | 18 | Meta Transparency Center (Community Standards, Advertising Standards), Meta Terms | copyrighted, used for non-commercial research only |
| TikTok policies | 3 | Branded Content Policy, Community Guidelines, ad creatives policy | copyrighted, research only |
| YouTube policies | 4 | Paid product placements, monetization policies, advertiser-friendly guidelines, Community Guidelines | copyrighted, research only |
| Regulations | 7 | FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255, eCFR), FTC influencer guides, ASA/CAP guide and Code sections 2 and 18, EU Digital Services Act | public domain (US) / EU reuse policy / ASA copyright |
| Contracts (real) | 100 | random sample (seed 42) of CUAD v1 full contract texts | CC BY 4.0 |
| Contracts (synthetic) | 20 | generated from a template + `contracts_index` | project-generated |
| Agency SOPs (synthetic) | 6 | written by hand (`data/sops/`) | project-generated |

13 documents have more than one snapshot (for example the FTC Endorsement Guides 2016 vs 2023, the TikTok
Branded Content Policy 2024 vs 2026, several Meta Community Standards 2024 vs 2026). Snapshots with the same
text are not counted as new versions during ingestion.

Known issues:
- Instagram help-center pages could not be used (JavaScript-only pages), see decisions.md #11
- the ASA influencer guide page is short: the full guide is a PDF that is not included
- the EU DSA is a very long legal text and produces many chunks compared to the other documents
- some archived snapshots were empty and are skipped by ingestion

## Clause classification dataset (`data/clauses/`)

- Built by `finetuning/build_dataset.py` from CUAD v1 (Atticus Project, CC BY 4.0, 510 contracts from SEC
  filings). Derived data, same license; please cite CUAD (Hendrycks et al., 2021) when reusing it.
- 10,025 sentences, 9 classes (8 clause types mapped from CUAD labels + "other"), split by contract:
  train 7,099 (356 contracts), val 1,544 (76), test 1,382 (77).
- "other" also contains 3 random un-annotated sentences per contract, which were not checked by a lawyer.

## Evaluation data (`eval/datasets/`)

All written by hand for this project, in English.

| file | n | content |
|---|---|---|
| `questions_v1.jsonl` | 137 | main set: policy, contract, sql, hybrid, action, unanswerable (see eval_protocol.md) |
| `questions_holdout.jsonl` | 12 | SQL + action questions written after the v2 fixes |
| `version_questions.jsonl` | 11 | questions answered only by an old snapshot of a document |
| `sql_safety.jsonl` | 28 | 18 unsafe SQL queries + 10 injection-style chat prompts |
| `compliance_captions.jsonl` | 60 | invented captions (29 compliant, 31 non-compliant) with the expected problems; brand names are the fictional brands of the synthetic DB |

Gold answers come from the stored document snapshots and the synthetic database; they say what the
documents said at snapshot time, not what the law is today.
